newsitem.title: UK: Chronology of events since end of IRA ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events since end of IRA ceasefire.

text.p: Following is a chronology of attacks in British-ruled Northern Ireland and on the mainland, and of police actions since the Irish Republican Army called off a 17-month ceasefire in February.
February 9, 1996 - A huge IRA bomb rocks London's Docklands commercial district, killing two and injuring 100. The blast came just minutes after the IRA declared its 17-month ceasefire was over.
February 15 - IRA bomb left in holdall in telephone box in Charing Cross Road, central London. Defused by police.
February 18 - An explosion ripped apart a bus in central London, killing the IRA guerrilla carrying it and injuring nine other people.
February 19 - Police find bomb-making equipment and explosives in London home of dead IRA bomber.
March 9 - A small IRA bomb exploded near West Brompton underground station in London. No injuries.
April 17 - A small IRA bomb exploded in exclusive part of Earl's Court district in west London. No injuries.
April 24 - Two huge bombs placed under London's Hammersmith bridge but failed to detonate. No one was injured by what police said were biggest devices planted by IRA in mainland Britain.
June 15 - IRA bomb in a van exploded in a shopping centre in northern English city of Manchester injuring over 200 people and devastating city centre.
June 28 - Three IRA mortars fired at British army barracks in Osnabruck, Germany. No injuries but several buildings badly damaged.

July 13 - Car bomb devastates the Kilyhelvin Hotel in the largely Protestant town of Enniskillen, injuring 17 people. The IRA denies it involved. Suspicion falls on the breakaway republican group, the Irish Continuity Army Council.
July 15 - Police arrest seven people in London and seize components for up to 36 bombs believed intended to target utilities installations in London and south-east England.

Sept 23 - Police arrest six people, one of whom killed in shootout, and seize large quantity of explosives, weapons and bomb-making equipment. Police say raids thwarted "serious, imminent IRA terrorist attack" on British mainland.
Sept 29 - A car bomb in Belfast made safe. Irish Continuity Army Council claims responsibility.

Oct 7 - Two bombs explode in the heart of the British army's headquarters at Lisburn, south of Belfast. Up to 20 people are injured. No group claims responsibility in the immediate aftermath of the blast.
